title: Spectroscopic fingerprints of a ferroaxial charge density wave
authors: Jiangchang Zheng, Zhongyi Zhang, Fazhi Yang, Josh Leeman, Luanjing Li, Zihan Lin, Zijian Fei, Tianhao Guo, Siyu Heng, Xin Liang, Leslie M. Schoop, Junzhang Ma, Hoi Chun Po, Berthold Jäck
abstract: Unconventional charge density waves (CDWs) with complex order parameters can host exotic collective modes and non-trivial topologies. They have emerged as a new frontier in the study of quantum matter. Recent experiments on rare-earth tritellurides have reported evidence for a ferroaxial CDW through the detection of characteristic Raman modes. This phase, often regarded as a hidden order, has been recognized to arise from the coupling between charge and orbital degrees of freedom in these materials. Yet, spectroscopic insight into its underlying electronic structure and the explicit form of its order parameter symmetry has remained elusive. Here, we present results from linearly polarized angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) and scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) measurements of the CDW phase in LaTe$_3$. Our ARPES measurements reveal a complex landscape of spectral gaps across the reconstructed Fermi surface, while our STM-based quasiparticle interference (QPI) mapping, enhanced through the selective deposition of atomic scattering centers, directly reveals an inter-orbital CDW with mixed $p_x$-$p_z$ orbital character. The detailed analysis of the QPI characteristics in terms of the order parameter symmetry within the orbital subspace of the Fermi surface suggests a mixed CDW phase with substantial ferroaxial component, which breaks all vertical mirror symmetries. More broadly, our work establishes a powerful spectroscopic pathway, based on scattering off individual atoms, for identifying and characterizing hidden, multi-component electronic orders in quantum materials using STM and ARPES measurements.
summary: The authors investigate the complex Charge Density Wave state in $	ext{LaTe}_3$ using both ARPES and advanced STM/QPI mapping. By analyzing how scattering patterns depend on orbital character, they determine that the CDW order parameter must possess a mixed, ferroaxial symmetry component. This establishes a robust spectroscopic pathway for characterizing exotic electronic orders in quantum materials.
main_problem: The primary goal is to spectroscopically characterize the symmetry and electronic structure of unconventional Charge Density Waves (CDWs), specifically focusing on the ferroaxial component in $	ext{LaTe}_3$. This requires distinguishing between intra-orbital and inter-orbital CDW order parameters.
main_result: The combination of ARPES and STM/QPI measurements strongly suggests a mixed, inter-orbital CDW phase characterized by a substantial ferroaxial component that breaks all vertical mirror symmetries. The QPI analysis successfully rules out purely conventional or intra-orbital models.
method: The study employs both experimental techniques (ARPES for band structure, STM/QPI mapping) and theoretical modeling using tight-binding Hamiltonians extended to include CDW order parameters ($\Delta_{	ext{CDW}}$).
model_or_system: The system is $	ext{LaTe}_3$, a rare-earth tritelluride exhibiting a complex CDW. The electronic structure is modeled in the $(p_x, p_z)$ orbital subspace using a $2 	imes 2$ matrix Hamiltonian to capture inter-orbital coupling.
key_observables: Spectral gaps across the Fermi surface (ARPES); Quasiparticle Interference (QPI) patterns and scattering vectors ($\mathbf{q}_1, \mathbf{q}_2, \mathbf{q}_3$) derived from 2D-FFT of STM $dI/dV$ maps.
important_parameters: The CDW order parameter $\Delta_{	ext{CDW}}$ is analyzed in terms of Pauli matrices ($\sigma_x, i\sigma_y$), distinguishing between intra-orbital and inter-orbital coupling strengths.
main_assumptions: The analysis approximates the incommensurate CDW using a nearby commensurate wave vector; the QPI signal calculation relies on the T-matrix formalism applied to the extended Hamiltonian.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate crystal structure, ARPES band folding due to CDW formation, and critically, STM/QPI maps showing characteristic cross-like features whose symmetry is mapped onto theoretical predictions for different CDW order parameter symmetries.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the experimental evidence (ARPES gaps, QPI modulation) of a complex CDW. It then uses detailed QPI analysis and theoretical modeling to constrain the possible symmetry components ($\sigma_x$ vs. $i\sigma_y$), ultimately concluding that only a mixed ferroaxial phase matches all observed spectroscopic fingerprints.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, multi-pronged spectroscopic methodology (combining ARPES and STM/QPI) to resolve ambiguities in the symmetry of hidden electronic orders like CDWs, which is highly relevant for understanding correlated electron physics beyond simple mean-field treatments.
